sentences.text: Zhongjianornis was a beaked bird roughly the size of a pigeon that lived in China during the early Cretaceous.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — is a nearly complete skeleton missing only a few tail vertebrae.
It possessed an expanded deltopectoral crest, a wing muscle attachment found in basal birds like Jeholornis, suggesting an early flight architecture.
The only known fossil was found at Jianchang in Liaoning Province within the Jiufotang Formation.
The species name Zhongjianornis yangi honors Yang Zhongjian, the founder of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, which holds the holotype.
Zhou, Zhang, and Li formally described the species in a paper published in January 2010, which had been available online since 2009.
Zhongjianornis is classified within the superorder Dinosauria, order Saurischia, suborder Theropoda, and unranked family Avialae.
Zhongjianornis lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous.
Initial analysis suggested Zhongjianornis was more primitive than Confuciusornis and lived before the evolutionary split between Euornithes and Enantiornithes.
It is debated whether Zhongjianornis is a very primitive bird, as later analyses cast doubt on its basal position.
A 2012 study argued that apparent primitive features were due to poor bone preservation and that its anatomy is actually more similar to primitive Euornithes like Chaoyangia and Schizooura.
Phylogenetic analysis indicates that a very primitive position for Zhongjianornis in the bird family tree is unlikely given current evidence.
